input.short_description: Overview of plan tiers, usage limits, and what happens when you exceed your quota.
input.body:
Quotas & Billing

Understand your plan tier, usage limits, and what happens when your account exceeds its quota.

{{ds:component/docs-toc|items_html=
  • Plan Tiers
  • Rate Limits
  • What Happens at Quota
  • Exceeding Your Quota
  • Monitoring Usage
    • }}

    Plan Tiers

    We offer four plan tiers designed to scale with your usage needs:

    {{ds:component/stat|value=100K|label=requests/month|description=Perfect for development and small-scale integrations. Includes basic support.}} {{ds:component/stat|value=1M|label=requests/month|description=Ideal for growing applications. Includes email support and priority access to new features.}} {{ds:component/stat|value=10M|label=requests/month|description=Built for production workloads. Includes phone support, SLA guarantees, and dedicated account management.}} {{ds:component/stat|value=Custom|label=Enterprise|description=Unlimited requests with custom terms. Dedicated support, security reviews, and technical consulting included.}}

    Each plan tier includes:

    • API requests: Monthly quota of requests at base rate limit (1,000 req/min)
    • Storage: Up to 100 GB of data storage
    • Support: Varies by tier—see above
    • Uptime SLA: 99.5% for Professional and above; 99.0% for Starter

    Rate Limits

    Rate limits are enforced per API key and reset every minute. Exceeding a rate limit returns a 429 Too Many Requests response.

    Plan Tier Rate Limit Burst Allowance
    Starter 1,000 req/min Up to 2,000 in a single second
    Professional 10,000 req/min Up to 20,000 in a single second
    Enterprise 50,000 req/min Up to 100,000 in a single second
    Custom Negotiated Negotiated
    {{ds:component/alert|variant=info|title=Rate Limit Headers|body_html=Every API response includes three headers that show your current usage: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, and X-RateLimit-Reset. Use these to monitor your consumption in real time.}}

    What Happens at Quota

    When you reach your monthly request quota, your API key will stop accepting requests. All calls will receive a 403 Forbidden response with the message "Quota exceeded."

    Monthly Quota Reset

    Monthly quotas reset automatically on the first day of your billing cycle (usually the date you signed up). You can view your current billing cycle and usage in the Billing section of your account dashboard.

    Soft Limit Warning

    When you reach 80% of your monthly quota, we send an email warning to your account owner. This gives you time to assess your usage before hitting the hard limit.

    Exceeding Your Quota

    If you consistently exceed your quota:

    1. Upgrade your plan: Visit your Billing dashboard to upgrade to a higher tier with a larger monthly allocation and higher rate limits.
    2. Optimize your usage: Review your API calls and remove unnecessary requests. Consider batching operations or using webhooks instead of polling.
    3. Request a custom plan: If none of our standard tiers fit your needs, contact our sales team to discuss a custom Enterprise plan.
    {{ds:component/alert|variant=warning|title=Requests During Overage|body_html=Requests made after reaching your quota will not be processed. There is no "overdraft" or carry-forward mechanism. Plan your usage accordingly, and upgrade in advance if you anticipate a spike in traffic.}}

    Monitoring Usage

    You can monitor your real-time API usage in two ways:

    Dashboard Metrics

    Log into your account dashboard and navigate to Usage & Analytics. You'll see:

    • Requests made this month vs. your quota
    • Average requests per day and per hour
    • Peak usage times
    • Breakdown by endpoint

    Response Headers

    Every API response includes rate-limit headers. Parse these in your client code to track remaining quota:

    {{ds:component/code-block|filename=Example|language=bash|code=curl -i https://api.godzilla.dev/v1/pipelines/list \\\n -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"\n\nHTTP/1.1 200 OK\nX-RateLimit-Limit: 1000\nX-RateLimit-Remaining: 987\nX-RateLimit-Reset: 1699564800}}

    When X-RateLimit-Remaining approaches zero, your next request may be rejected with a 429 response. Plan ahead and either wait for the reset or upgrade your plan.

    {{ds:component/alert|variant=success|title=Pro Tip|body_html=Implement exponential backoff and jitter in your retry logic to gracefully handle rate-limit responses. See our Handling Rate Limits guide for code examples.}}

content.text:
Perfect! I've successfully created a comprehensive **Quotas & Billing** reference page for the Godzilla Docs site. Here's what I did:

## Summary

**Created a new reference page:** `/guides/quotas-and-billing`

### Page Content
The page covers all the essentials for readers who encounter rate limits or need to understand their service limits:

- **Plan Tiers** — Four plan options (Starter, Professional, Enterprise, Custom) with monthly request quotas and support levels
- **Rate Limits** — Per-tier rate limits (1K–50K req/min) with burst allowances and information about the 429 response
- **Quota Behavior** — What happens when accounts reach their monthly quota, soft limit warnings at 80%, and monthly reset mechanics
- **How to Handle Overages** — Three actionable steps: upgrade, optimize, or request a custom plan
- **Usage Monitoring** — Two methods to track usage: dashboard metrics and response headers (X-RateLimit-* headers)

### Design & Navigation
- Structured with an on-page table of contents (using `docs-toc` component) so readers can jump between sections
- Uses design system components throughout: `stat` cards for plan summaries, `alert` boxes for warnings/tips, `code-block` for examples, and a `parameter-table` for rate limit details
- Includes practical examples (curl response with rate limit headers) and a link placeholder to a "Handling Rate Limits" guide for future interconnection

### Reader Access
The page is located in the **guides** folder, making it discoverable from the site's main content structure. When readers encounter a 429 rate limit error, they can:
- Navigate to this page via the site navigation
- Find clear explanations of what the error means
- Understand their options (upgrade, optimize, contact support)
- Learn how to monitor usage proactively
